gaps.sentence: Little ___ the chances of success be improved by patience.
gaps.explanation: Little will the chances be improved… — inversion with future.

gaps.sentence: Never before that afternoon ___ so many goals been scored in one match.
gaps.explanation: 'Never before that afternoon' fixes the reference in the past: had so many goals been scored.

gaps.sentence: No sooner ___ the contract been signed than problems arose.
gaps.explanation: Past perfect passive with inversion: had … been signed.

gaps.sentence: Not since the winter of 1963 ___ temperatures dropped so low.
gaps.explanation: 'Not since 1963 have temperatures dropped …' — the only time from then until now.

gaps.sentence: Not until the film ended ___ anybody speak.
gaps.explanation: Not until + time clause at the front: did anybody speak.

gaps.sentence: Only after the third reminder ___ she reply to my email.
gaps.explanation: 'Only after' fronts the condition, so 'did she reply' inverts.

gaps.sentence: Not once ___ she mentioned the incident to anyone.
gaps.explanation: 'Not once has she mentioned' — inversion with the perfect.

gaps.sentence: So ferocious ___ the storm prove that three coastal villages were evacuated.
gaps.explanation: With the bare verb 'prove', the inversion takes do-support: did the storm prove.
